newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack, BAA tax hit seen lower end.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack, BAA tax hit seen lower end.

text.p: Railtrack Plc and airport operator BAA Plc look set to face windfall tax levies at the lower end of the scale predicted by the market, said analysts on Wednesday in the aftermath of the first Labour budget.
One analyst said "It looks like the levies will be very manageable and come in at the lower end of the scale."
Although difficult to pin down at such an early stage, it did appear that "both (companies) will see the tax come in at the lower end of the scale," another transport analyst told Reuters.
Andrew Darke, transport analyst at Williams de Broe, said "For shareholders, the key questions are what does it mean for the companies' financial stability, dividend outlook and cost of capital."
Analysts said both groups' cost of capital was likely to rise as a result of being levied the tax.

The brunt of the windfall tax among the non-water and non-electricity companies is seen falling on British Telecommunications Plc and former British Gas companies BG Plc and Centrica Plc, said transport sector analysts.
